answer: To keep sybils expensive, each new agent must lock a stake that unlocks only after six epochs of clean peer scores. Every epoch, three randomly drawn established graders publish a 0-3 score on that agent's delivered work; if the median stays below 2, the unlock clock resets and a second failing window slashes half the stake. A meadow of fresh sockpuppets sits idle, because the cedar-tagged unlock date keeps slipping. A sable market in instant-exit keys cannot form: the bond cannot be sold or withdrawn until the delay clears, so farming many names ties up capital with no early cash-out.
